sources.entry: beautifulsoup4 - Providing Pythonic idioms for iterating, searching, and modifying HTML or XML.

summary.name: Beautiful Soup
summary.one_liner: Beautiful Soup is a Python library for pulling data out of HTML and XML files, providing idiomatic ways to navigate, search, and modify the parse tree.
use_cases: Extracting all links from a web page
Pulling text content out of HTML files
Searching for tags by name, attribute, or CSS class
Porting code from Beautiful Soup 3 to 4
summary.what_it_does: The library parses HTML or XML into a tree of Python objects (Tag, NavigableString, BeautifulSoup, Comment) that can be navigated by tag, parent, and sibling relationships. Its find() and find_all() methods accept filters based on tag name, attributes, string content, regular expressions, lists, or custom functions. Tags and attributes can be read, added, changed, or deleted, and get_text() extracts the text of a page. It works with several parsers, including Python's built-in html.parser, lxml, and html5lib, and the page notes that different parsers can produce different trees for invalid markup.
notable: Works with multiple parsers (html.parser, lxml, html5lib) and an XML mode
Flexible search filters: names, attributes, regex, lists, and custom functions
Multi-valued attributes such as class are stored as lists by default
Documentation covers Beautiful Soup 4.15.0 and is translated into several languages
caveats: Beautiful Soup 3 is no longer developed and support was dropped on December 31, 2020
The page notes that the examples were written for Python 3.8, and the author develops with Python 3.10
Parser choice affects output: invalid documents can produce different trees depending on the parser
